answer: A congestion-pricing prism for agent identity meters each agent's transaction flow across shared channels, charging escalating tolls when one credential floods the network. Every new agent voyage pays a capacity reservation fee plus a decayed trust budget inherited from its sponsor, so mass registration shifts cost onto the attacker's own ledger. Spoofed identities then congest their own ocean of quotas, forcing either real collateral outlay or throttled throughput, though colluding sponsors with deep reserves can still subsidize a slow swarm under the toll ceiling.
